summary.headline: Prioritise service revenue over speculative SaaS; current official evidence supports a focused SME cyber-hygiene offer, while buyer demand still needs validation.
summary.best_opportunity: Fixed-scope cyber-hygiene and phishing-readiness setup for small UK businesses, with a modest monthly check-in.
summary.why_now: The UK Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025 reports 43% of businesses identified a breach or attack in the prior 12 months; phishing remains the most prevalent and disruptive incident type. This is a need signal, not proof of willingness to buy: https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/cyber-security-breaches-survey-2025/cyber-security-breaches-survey-2025

top_opportunities.name: SME cyber-hygiene and phishing-readiness setup
top_opportunities.description: A bounded, non-penetration-testing service: MFA and backup checks, account-recovery review, staff phishing-response checklist, basic policy/action register and referral to qualified security providers for deeper work.
top_opportunities.why_now: The 2025 UK government survey reports 43% of businesses identified a breach or attack in the previous 12 months; phishing was the most prevalent and disruptive. Survey prevalence does not establish local buying intent.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small professional-services firms, charities and owner-managed businesses without in-house IT/security staff.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£900 for training, insurance/legal review, demo materials and basic tooling; do not offer specialist testing without competence and cover.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks through paid readiness reviews and local IT/accountant referrals; validate first.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium: £50–£200/month for scheduled checks and staff refreshers, contingent on demonstrated value.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good for technical implementation and automation; security competence, trust and scope discipline are essential.
risks: Avoid claiming certification, guaranteed protection or performing intrusive testing outside competence and written authorisation.
High trust barrier and crowded MSP/security market; survey evidence measures incidents, not service purchasing.
top_opportunities.verdict: Test as a tightly scoped readiness service and refer technical remediation to qualified partners; do not build SaaS first.

top_opportunities.name: SME workflow automation implementation
top_opportunities.description: Audited, fixed-scope automation for repetitive admin: enquiry triage, appointment reminders, document intake and CRM updates.
top_opportunities.why_now: UK has 5.64m small businesses; ample prospect pool, but no retrieved evidence establishes local AI buying intent.
top_opportunities.buyer: Owner-operated service firms and small professional practices with repeated admin and lead follow-up.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£1,000 for demos, API usage and basic insurance/legal review.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–4 weeks through paid workflow audit and one implementation.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High if monitoring and improvements are retained (£100–£500/month), not guaranteed.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong for a software engineer who can integrate existing tools and demonstrate measurable time savings.
risks: Scope creep, fragile integrations and handling personal data create delivery and compliance risk.
Crowded market; generic AI positioning lacks differentiation.
top_opportunities.verdict: Sell a paid, measurable pilot in one vertical; do not build a platform first.

top_opportunities.name: Local-business lead response & booking service
top_opportunities.description: Managed website forms, missed-call text-back, booking and review follow-up for one local service niche.
top_opportunities.why_now: Large small-business base supports prospecting; opportunity depends on proving missed enquiries and conversion economics in a chosen locality.
top_opportunities.buyer: Trades, clinics, salons or other appointment-led businesses with slow enquiry response.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300–£1,200 using existing booking, messaging and website tools.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks if sold as setup plus monthly management.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High potential via monthly service contract.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good engineering fit; sales and local prospecting are the main constraints.
risks: Attribution is difficult and client lead volumes may be low.
Messaging consent, platform rules and deliverability must be handled correctly.
top_opportunities.verdict: Offer one niche a low-risk 30-day pilot with a clear response-time and booking metric.

top_opportunities.name: Niche website care & conversion service
top_opportunities.description: Maintain and improve websites for a specific local-business vertical: speed, forms, booking, accessibility basics and monthly reporting.
top_opportunities.why_now: Recurring operational need and broad SME population; public evidence gathered here does not quantify unmet website-service demand.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small businesses relying on a dated or poorly converting website.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £150–£700 for hosting, monitoring, templates and outreach.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks via fixed-price audits and repairs.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong; low-cost technical delivery, but differentiation and prospecting matter.
risks: Commodity pricing from agencies and DIY platforms.
Client approvals and unclear content responsibilities slow delivery.
top_opportunities.verdict: Choose a vertical and bundle maintenance with one concrete conversion improvement.

top_opportunities.name: Vertical micro-SaaS for compliance/admin
top_opportunities.description: A small workflow tool for one underserved UK niche, discovered by manually delivering the process first and converting repeated work into software.
top_opportunities.why_now: The large SME population offers potential buyers, but live evidence in this run does not validate a particular unmet software gap.
top_opportunities.buyer: A narrow professional or trade niche with a repeated, costly administrative task.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £500–£2,000 for a lean prototype, hosting and customer discovery.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Usually slower (4–12+ weeks); seek paid design partners before coding.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High potential subscription revenue if retention is established.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong technical fit; market discovery and distribution are critical risks.
risks: Building before confirming willingness to pay wastes scarce time and budget.
Incumbents, integrations and regulatory requirements can expand scope.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not start with code; obtain three paid pilot commitments for one narrowly defined workflow.

best_pick.name: SME cyber-hygiene and phishing-readiness setup
best_pick.why_it_wins: It maps to a current government-reported business pain and can be delivered as a small paid service without product development. Evidence is directional; customer interviews and paid pilots must establish demand and competence fit.
validation_plan: Speak with 8 local small-business owners and 3 independent IT/MSP providers to learn current controls, unmet needs and referral boundaries.
Offer three paid, fixed-scope reviews; proceed only if customers pay and an experienced security practitioner validates the checklist and service boundaries.
best_pick.first_offer: £199 fixed-scope cyber-hygiene review with written prioritised actions; no penetration testing, certification or guarantee.
best_pick.mvp: A documented checklist, client-authorised evidence review, concise action report and optional quarterly follow-up; use established tools and avoid storing credentials.
customer_types: Small professional-services firms without in-house IT
best_pick.do_today: Read the 2025 government survey and interview three local business owners plus one MSP; verify qualifications, insurance and scope before offering security advice.
